title: Can You Tell?
logline: A street host runs a blind sip test on a college quad: sugar or no sugar? Everyone, including a chemistry professor, says sugar. The sleeve comes off: it's {product}.

fictional_brands: Quad Talk (the host's street interview channel, on the mic flag and the end card, added in post)

ingested.moment: blind sip from a plain sample cup poured from the sleeved can, then the sleeve comes off (the kraft sleeve and sample cups are generic: any product can hide under a plain paper cover)

applied.moment: blind test on the back of the hand (a lotion, balm or sunscreen from a sleeved tube): guess the thing it's missing, then the sleeve comes off

worn.moment: they try it on without seeing the label (glasses, a jacket, shoes) and guess the price or what's missing, then the reveal

handheld.moment: they use the sleeved gadget for five seconds (earbuds, a bottle, a tool) and guess, then the reveal

carried.moment: they lift the covered bag or case and guess the weight or price, then the cover comes off

home.moment: they sit on or switch on the covered item set up on the quad (a chair, a lamp, a blanket) and guess, then the cover comes off

consumable.moment: they taste or smell a sample from the unmarked refill pack and guess, then the pack is revealed

beats.summary: Bea straight into the lens on the quad, sleeved can and sample cups in hand: sugar or no sugar?
Three quick blind sips, three confident answers: sugar. The chemistry professor is the most certain.
Bea slides the kraft sleeve off the can: Red Bull Sugarfree, made without sugar. Tyler's jaw drops.
Mei checks what it means; Bea gives the allowed claim. The professor takes a can for his 8am.
A line of people has formed behind them wanting to try.
Bea holds the can next to the mic flag, tagline, and calls the next person in.

lore: The quad is the old heart of a fictional East Coast college: the chemistry hall on the north side went up in 1911, the maples along the path were planted by the class of 1962, and the path is worn smooth down the middle by a century of short cuts.
Bea has run Quad Talk for three years and 212 episodes, filmed on one phone by her roommate Dani. Her record is 41 interviews in a single afternoon.

Today's blind test: 30 plain sample cups, one can hidden in a sleeve Bea folded from a grocery bag and taped shut with sky-blue washi tape. The chalk tally board says every taster so far has guessed sugar.
Dr. Harold Greene has taught intro chemistry here for 34 years and has a standing bet with his students that he can name any sweetener by taste. He has never lost it.
It is the Thursday of midterm week: half the quad is running on no sleep, and homecoming pennants are already up for Saturday.
